Custom orchestration.description: Generic bucket for self-built multi-agent orchestration: custom skills, scripts, message buses, dispatchers and swarms that commenters wrote themselves to coordinate several coding agents.

Herdr.description: Open-source runtime and workspace for running many coding agents: a native desktop app (macOS, Linux, Windows) plus the original terminal multiplexer TUI, with per-pane agent status and a socket API; agents run in a local herdr-core server.

Subagents (built-in).description: Generic bucket for the built-in subagent features of coding harnesses (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, Pi plugins) where the main agent spawns child agents for subtasks.

Git worktrees.description: Git's worktree feature (multiple checked-out working directories from one repo), widely used to run parallel coding agents on separate branches without conflicts.

Muse.description: Meta's Muse AI family: the Muse Spark/Glimmer models, the Muse personal agent app, and Muse Code, Meta's coding agent with monthly plans starting at $5/month. Commenters used it as a coding model/subscription and personal assistant.

tmux / zellij.description: Terminal multiplexers (tmux and Zellij) used to run and switch between many agent sessions in panes/windows that persist in the background.

Rex.description: Combined native terminal emulator and multiplexer (built on libghostty) from Mitchell Hashimoto's company Superlogical, with built-in sessions, splits and persistence; macOS client in public testing since Oct 2026.

cmux.description: Open-source Ghostty-based native macOS terminal for running multiple AI coding agents, with vertical workspace tabs, notifications when agents need input, and a CLI/socket API.

OpenRig.description: Open-source tool for building persistent teams of Claude Code, Codex and Pi agents with roles, shared context and owned work, running in tmux.

Cloud agents.description: Generic bucket for cloud-hosted coding agents that run in isolated remote environments (e.g. vendor cloud/background agents) or on schedules; the specific service was not named.

Ctlflow.description: System for running a self-defined fleet of AI agents locally that people talk to through Matrix chat rooms, with a server (crossfire), local controller (fleetd) and CLI (fleet).

Conductor.description: Mac app for running parallel Claude Code, Codex and Cursor agents in isolated git-worktree workspaces and reviewing/merging their changes, by Melty Labs.

Gas Town.description: Steve Yegge's open-source multi-agent workspace manager for coordinating many Claude Code-style agents on a codebase.

Raven.description: EverMind AI's open-source 'harness of harnesses' that plans tasks as a dependency graph and delegates nodes to its own agents or to third-party harnesses like Claude Code and Codex (via ACP/CLI/APIs); pre-alpha.

agent-swarm.dev.description: Agent Swarm: MIT-licensed, self-hostable multi-agent system where a lead agent delegates goals to worker agents such as Claude Code or Codex; a paid hosted cloud version also exists. By Desplega Labs.

LangGraph.description: LangChain's open-source framework for building stateful, graph-structured LLM agents and multi-agent workflows.

Collie.description: Open-source iOS app for remotely controlling Herdr-managed coding agents (used over Tailscale).

Contextify.description: macOS companion app for Claude Code and Codex CLI that monitors coding sessions with a timeline and LLM summaries, letting past session context be reused.

Open Agent Harness (OAH).description: Open-source multi-agent development harness for macOS and Windows that coordinates Claude Code and Codex, with file leases and task history.

OpenCode swarm plugins.description: Generic bucket for community plugins that add multi-agent/swarm orchestration to the OpenCode coding agent.

yaac.description: Open-source tool by the commenter that auto-containerizes coding agents (gVisor containers) and provides inter-agent orchestration.

Helyn Implement.description: Unidentified; the commenter describes it as a multi-model agentic protocol/workflow used for coding. No public product found.

Munder Difflin.description: Open-source local multi-agent harness that runs an 'office' of Claude Code/Codex-style agents on your laptop or sandboxes using existing subscriptions.

Muster.description: Open-source native macOS workspace for AI coding agents built on libghostty, with real splits, agent state at a glance, local and SSH agents, and sessions that outlive the app.

Scion.description: Google Cloud's experimental open-source orchestrator that runs multiple coding agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex) in parallel, each in its own container with separate credentials and git worktree.

clawpatrol.description: Deno's open-source security firewall/proxy for AI agents that enforces action-approval rules and manages credentials.

Paseo / Orca / Superset.description: Group of 'harness aggregator' apps for running multiple coding agents in parallel: Paseo (desktop and mobile), Orca by Stably AI (desktop/mobile/remote, MIT) and Superset (superset.sh).

Fizzy.description: Kanban board app from 37signals/Basecamp, source-available and self-hostable; the commenter runs it locally to track and delegate work to agents.

Hangar.description: Open-source, self-hosted app that puts Claude Code, Codex, Pi, omp and Kimi Code agents in one place, on desktop and phone.

Command Center.description: Commenter's own product; most likely Command Center, a desktop AI coding environment on top of Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode with review and parallel workspace management (founder Jimmy Koppel). Not definitively matched.

Circus Chief.description: Open-source meta-harness for orchestrating Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and Gemini CLI agents, with subscription fallback tiers; published on npm.

Codealong.description: Free, open-source macOS/Linux app that shows every coding agent you run (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity, Cursor) in one window across accounts and machines.

Agent Orchestrator.description: Unspecified 'agent orchestrator' listed without detail; possibly a generic orchestrator or a product such as Agent Orchestrator (orchestrator.inc). Not identifiable from the comment.

DevArch.description: Commercial layer for Claude Code that adds directives, agents, hooks and skills to enforce engineering discipline (quality gates, session continuity, ADRs), by David Cornelson; paid annual license.

agentcron.ai.description: AgentCron, a team collaboration workspace (chat, projects/kanban, docs, files) usable with AI agents such as ChatGPT, Claude and Grok, e.g. via MCP.

epiq.description: Open-source, Git-native distributed issue tracker and workflow manager for agentic teams, with a terminal UI and no server or account needed.

Belfry.description: Open-source native macOS/iOS front-end for tmux showing hosts, sessions and windows in a sidebar with the live terminal, locally or over SSH; by Rob Gough.

Paperclip.description: Open-source app for managing AI agents at work, coordinating multiple agents on tasks.

Termic.description: Open-source (AGPL) Conductor.build alternative that runs the real Claude, Gemini and Codex CLIs in real terminals for switching between parallel agents.

Briefkin.description: Hosted dashboard and notification service where coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, scripts) report progress and blockers to a card board, with Telegram alerts when input is needed; in open beta.

Kiro Crew.description: Open-source companion to Amazon's Kiro providing a persistent, self-improving workspace with background subagents, scheduled jobs and persistent memory that continues beyond one session.

LoopX.description: Open-source, local-first control plane and research workbench for long-running agent teams that span multiple sessions and runtimes.

CrewAI.description: Open-source Python framework (and commercial platform) for orchestrating role-playing autonomous AI agents that collaborate on tasks.

agent-chat.description: The commenter's own (unreleased or unpublicized) product in which writer agents and cross-model-family reviewer agents collaborate; no public listing found.
